site.tagline: Measurements of hardware MIDI sound modules
site.lede: What the instrument answered, not what the manual says.
site.description: An archive of what hardware MIDI sound modules actually do: which addresses answer, what values they take, what a reset puts back, and which of them change the sound. Measured on specific units, one at a time.

landing.what: Every address of one sound module is read, written to, reset and listened to, one at a time, and only what came back is written down. Nothing is copied from a specification, and a question that was never put is left as a gap rather than filled in.
landing.coverage: {addresses} addresses answered a read. {powerOn} of them held a value at power-on. {listened} were listened to, and {heard} of those changed the sound.
landing.mapBody: Every address the unit answered a read at: what it held at power-on, what values it took, whether its neighbours are separate addresses, and what each reset put back.
landing.cataloguesBody: The bank and program combinations the unit actually moved to, and the insertion effect types it stored — with what each effect's parameters were heard to do.
landing.emulatorBody: A model of the control surface driven by the measurements alone. It answers what was recorded, and says so when a question was never put.
landing.observationsBody: What the unit did that no address explains: a read of 256 bytes that stops it answering, a reply that runs on for 29 seconds. Each says how it was found and what it does not establish.
landing.caveat: Every finding here belongs to one unit, measured on one path, on the day it was taken. It is not a statement about a model, a firmware revision, or anyone else's unit. Where a run never reached something, the page says so rather than filling the gap in.

terms.address: Three seven-bit bytes naming one byte of the unit's parameter space.
terms.region: A run of addresses the unit answered a single read at.
terms.block: The first two bytes of an address. The site shards its data by it.
terms.bank: The top byte of an address.
terms.rq1-dt1: The two Roland system-exclusive messages this archive uses: RQ1 asks for bytes, DT1 writes them.
terms.sweep: The stage that maps which addresses answer at all, and what they held when asked.
terms.power-on-value: What the address held immediately after a power cycle, before anything but a read was sent.
terms.boundary: The stage that reads past a region's mapped end, and on while anything still answers.
terms.write-probe: The stage that measures what an address accepts: a ladder of values written one at a time and read back.
terms.hold-probe: The stage that tells a store from a window, by giving a whole run different values before reading any of them back.
terms.resets: What each of the unit's resets put back, read against a mark written into every writable address first.
terms.window: A block with no storage of its own: reading or writing here reaches an address in another block instead.
terms.alias: A MIDI message measured to land in this address. It says where a value is kept, not that anything uses it.
terms.stimulus: A named note — program, pitch, velocity, hold time — used to ask whether a parameter changes the sound.
terms.repeatability: How closely two takes of one setting agree. Every audible verdict is read against it.
terms.audible: Two settings sounded different by more than the unit fails to repeat itself by. Not that it is useful.
terms.superseded: A verdict a later record replaced. Both are kept, and the superseded one is shown dimmed.
terms.insertion-effect: An effect placed in a part's signal path, selected by writing a two-byte type number.
terms.map-select: One of the alternative tone maps a bank-select LSB chooses between.

search.hint: Type an address, a byte of one, or the name of a MIDI message.
search.noMatch: Nothing in this unit answers to that.
search.noMatchHint: The archive holds only what has been measured. An address absent here is one no run has reached, which is not the same as one the unit does not have.
search.tryHint: These are messages the archive measured landing in an address. Pick one to see where it went.

address.title: Address {address}
address.powerOnAlso: {value} when the space was asked in another shape
address.windowAgainst: Measured against {stores}, and against nothing else
address.windowWriteReached: A write through this address reached {address}
address.notContiguous: The probe writes a ladder of values rather than all 128, so this is what it accepted of what it tried.
address.window: This block has no storage of its own
address.windowBody: Blocks {blocks} hold nothing. Reading or writing an address in one of them reaches {onto} instead — whichever of the two was addressed last. The write points it there and the read follows, so an address here answers with whatever it was just given and looks like a store. Everything below describes what is being reached through it, not a store of its own.
address.notMeasuredBody: No run has put this question to this address. That is an absence in the archive, not a finding about the unit.
address.alsoIn: {count} more records establish the same thing
address.notInARegion: No sweep found a region here
address.askedAsARun: asked as a run of {length} from {start}

map.title: Address map
map.emptyBank: No region in this bank has been measured yet.
map.windowBlocks: {count} blocks of this unit hold nothing of their own

grid.body: One cell is one block, laid out at the byte it is addressed by: the column is its low nibble and the row its high one. The two grids are the same squares read twice — what the archive measured, and what a document states about the same place. A filled cell has something behind it and the fill says how much of the block that something covers; a hollow cell has nothing behind it, which is not the same as a block that answered nothing.
grid.pick: Select a cell to open the block behind it.
grid.gap: States rows the archive has no address for
grid.unstatedBank: No document read so far names an address in this bank.
grid.cellGap: {cell} — {count} stated rows the archive has no address for
grid.joined: Stated, and joined to a measurement
grid.offsetUnmatched: {address}: {parameter}, which the archive has no record of

tones.title: Tones
tones.lede: Every bank and program the unit moved to when it was asked for one. A combination it does not have is discarded, so a part that moved is the tone existing.
tones.mapsNote: A map select is another way of asking for this unit's tones, not another set of them: the same tone answers under more than one. The maps are counted separately below and are not added up.
tones.findHint: The bank and program numbers as the tables below give them. Each map select is answered separately, because the same pair can be a different tone under each.
tones.didNotMove: asked, and the part did not move
tones.notSwept: this bank was not asked for every program
tones.noBank: no bank of this number answered

effects.title: Insertion effects
effects.lede: Every type number the unit stored verbatim, with the settings it loads and what each of its parameters was heard to do.
effects.noParameters: This type's parameters have not been asked.

emulator.title: Emulator
emulator.lede: A model of the unit's control surface, driven entirely by the measurements. It answers what the archive recorded and says so when a question was never put — it does not guess.
emulator.inputHint: Hex bytes, or pick a message below.
emulator.unmeasured: Not measured, so nothing is claimed
emulator.marked: A marked message reaches something the observations page describes.

unit.lede: One physical unit, measured on one path, on the days these runs were taken. What follows is how much of it has been reached, what was asked of it, what stood between it and the archive, and how the measuring itself checked out.
unit.coverageLede: How much of the address space each question was actually put to. The whole is every address that answered a read at all; a bar that stops short is a run that stopped, not a unit that ends there.
unit.reachedByAMessage: Reached by a named MIDI message
unit.ofListened: {heard} of the {listened} listened to changed the sound. {notHeard} did not — which is a finding about the note it was asked with as much as about the address.
unit.stagesLede: Each is one command that produced records, and each puts a different question to the same unit. An underlined name has an entry in the glossary.
unit.chainLede: What stood between the instrument and the archive. A measurement is of a unit through a path, and the path is part of the finding.
unit.healthLede: What the chain was checked against while it ran. These are readings on the measuring, not on the unit.
unit.observationsLede: What the unit did that no address map would tell you. Each carries the method that established it and, in the same weight of type, what it does not establish — the limits are part of the finding rather than a footnote to it.

common.loadFailed: That part of the archive could not be loaded.
common.notAffiliated: Not affiliated with, or endorsed by, any instrument manufacturer. Product names identify the equipment measured.

claims.widthBody: The document says this parameter is {bytes} bytes wide. The write probe writes one byte at a time, so what it found here is about one byte of it and is not the same quantity.
claims.unresolved: The row continues onto a second line whose column the extraction could not settle: {cells}
claims.absentBody: Addresses this block's document states and the archive holds no record of. Nobody asked about them; that is not the same as asking and hearing nothing.

verdict.qualified: carries a note, so it settles on no one value
verdict.not asked: this reset was not asked about it
verdict.wider than was measured: wider than the byte measured, so not comparable
verdict.stated in words rather than as a value: stated in words rather than as a value

claims.title: Against the documentation
claims.rule: Everything on this page is evidence that a page of a published document stated something. That is a different kind of claim from a measurement, and it is never treated as one: where the document is silent, or where nothing has been measured, the answer is that one side said nothing — never that they differ, and never that the missing side is zero.
claims.notHosted: The document is not distributed here and no licence over it is granted or claimed. Each citation names the edition and the number printed on the page, which is what a reader holding their own copy needs to check it.
claims.noneDiffer: Nothing the document states and the archive measured disagrees. Many claims cannot be compared at all: the document is silent, nothing has been measured, or the two sides are not describing the same quantity. None of those is agreement, so each facet below counts them as verdicts of their own rather than folding them into a single number.
claims.someDiffer: {count} claim(s) state something the archive measured differently. A difference is worth doubting before it is worth reporting: check the block page, and check that both sides are speaking about the same quantity.
claims.absentSummary: {rows} rows of the document's tables, covering {addresses} addresses, state something no measurement has been held against. Nobody asked about them; that is not the same as asking and hearing nothing. This is the list to measure from.
claims.tableNotesBody: Notes the document attaches to a whole table rather than to one row. None carries a verdict: each states what a parameter does or what a message leaves behind, and the archive holds no reading that either agrees with it or does not.
claims.howItWasRead: Which rows it was taken to reach
claims.noneRead: No document has been read for this unit.
claims.browseBody: The tallies above say how many claims came out each way. This is the list behind them: pick a verdict to see the addresses that produced it, or search for the one you came for. One facet at a time — a claim is compared twice and the two fail differently, so a row here is one comparison and says which.
claims.showingFirst: showing the first {count}; narrow the search for the rest
claims.noneMatched: Nothing matched. That is a statement about the filter, not about the unit.
